content.text: In-class paired programming with AI assistance
Build a personality quiz while learning about JavaScript async timing

All the kids are doing it these days. This is where we'll learn a little bit about making interactive sites. We won't need to deal with any backend servers, just some nice clientside code to build up a fun quiz and show some calculated results.
Head over to buzzfeed and take
Doesn't that make you want to make your own quiz? Ok, you could use buzzfeed to do this, but you want to make one that doesn't have ugly ads. And looks classier too!
exercise. One computer, two people, taking turns driving. You'll be using Claude Code to help build the quiz - but pay attention, it might not always write perfect code on the first try!
This lab is designed differently than most. Here's the flow:
Work with Claude to implement the quiz functionality
When things break (they will!), investigate why with Claude's help
Apply fixes, understand the concepts, add finishing touches
When you hit bugs, don't just ask Claude to fix them immediately. Take time to understand
to trace what's happening. This debugging experience is the actual learning!

JavaScript timing can be tricky. You might encounter situations where:
Data seems to be missing when you try to use it
Elements can't be found even though they're in your HTML
Open the browser DevTools console (F12 or Cmd+Option+I)
Ask Claude questions like "Why might this variable be undefined here?"
By the end of this lab, you should understand:
Why JavaScript doesn't always run top-to-bottom
How to properly wait for data to load
When it's safe to access HTML elements
How to use console.log and DevTools to trace issues
Make sure your code is committed and pushed
Verify your quiz works in the browser

Feel free to suggest other possibilities; always mention extra credit in your submission.
